title: The normalization of a domain of finite type over Z is finite
statement: Let $A$ be an integral domain which is generated as a ring by finitely many elements, i.e. $\mathbf Z\to A$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], with field of fractions $K$, and let $A'=\{x\in K: x$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A\}$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Then $A'$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 0335 (proposition-ubiquity-nagata), items (3) and (5): Z and rings of finite type over Z are Nagata, in particular universally Japanese; Definition Tag 032R (definition-nagata (1): universally Japanese means every domain of finite type over the ring is N-2) and Definition Tag 032F (definition-N: N-2 with the trivial extension L = K gives N-1, i.e. the integral closure in K is finite). Used in the proof of Lemma Tag 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up): 'As R_0 is a Nagata domain we see that its integral closure R_0' is finite over R_0'

proof.text: Prove the Nagata condition for any ring R ring-isomorphic to the integers, hence for ULift.{u} ℤ. Transport the Noetherian, integrally closed and dimension-at-most-one instances from ℤ. For a nonzero prime p, dimension one makes p maximal, so R/p is a field. Its canonical fraction field is linearly equivalent to itself; a finite extension L of that fraction field is finite over R/p by transitivity. The integral closure is an R/p-submodule of this finite-dimensional space, hence is Noetherian and finite. For p = 0, identify R/(0) with ℤ. It is normal Noetherian and has characteristic zero; the fraction field has characteristic zero and the finite extension is separable (Mathlib instances PerfectField.ofCharZero and Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isSeparable_of_perfectField). Apply IsIntegralClosure.finite [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite]. This proves IsNagataRing R [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. These two branches are implemented by the fully proved private helpers isN2_field and isNagataRing_of_equiv_int.

proof.text: Equip A with the ULift.{u} ℤ-algebra structure by composing the original integer algebra map with ULift.ringEquiv. The scalar tower ℤ → ULift ℤ → A follows from multiplication associativity, and Algebra.FiniteType.of_restrictScalars_finiteType preserves finite type. Apply isUniversallyJapanese_of_isNagataRing [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-universally-japanese] to the lifted integer ring proved Nagata in step 1, then evaluate the universally Japanese condition [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] at A. Obtain IsN2 A (FractionRing A) [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. No universe or binder of the statement is changed.

proof.text: Apply IsN2 A (FractionRing A) directly to the trivial extension L = FractionRing A, whose finite-dimensional and scalar-tower instances are available. Thus Module.Finite A (integralClosure A (FractionRing A)). The canonical fraction-field equivalence FractionRing.algEquiv A K induces an A-algebra equivalence of integral closures by AlgEquiv.mapIntegralClosure. Transport Module.Finite along its underlying linear equivalence using Module.Finite.equiv. This gives the required finiteness in the specified arbitrary-universe fraction field K without using the still-sorry helper isN1_of_isN2.

split_report.summary: Mathlib has no Nagata / Japanese ring theory and no finiteness of the normalization of a domain of finite type over Z (or over a field); the only finiteness of integral closure is IsIntegralClosure.finite (Noetherian integrally closed base, finite separable extension). So the item is split along the Stacks route of its source, Proposition 0335 (3),(5): step 1 proves Z is a Nagata ring as in the proof of 0335 (F_p fields trivially N-2; Z normal Noetherian of characteristic 0, so N-2 by 032M/032L, the latter a new Mathlib leaf IsIntegralClosure.finite, separability from the existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable); step 2 applies Nagata's theorem 0334 (1)=>(3) (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-nagata-universally-japanese, the hard part: analytically unramified local rings) to get A N-2; step 3 takes L = K. Statement unchanged in content; stmt_deps were empty and now cite the new leaf definitions def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra (Algebra.FiniteType) and def-weil-pbc-integral-closure (integralClosure), and def-weil-finitely-generated-module. New definitions def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain (032F, N-1/N-2) and def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring (032R) are unsplit (no Mathlib counterpart). A direct route via Noether normalization was considered and rejected: over Z it only works after inverting an integer, and the points of mixed characteristic need exactly the Nagata machinery.
